title: How to Choose Custom MMA Shorts for Your Brand, Gym, or Team
description: Learn how to choose custom MMA shorts by fabric, fit, split, waistband, liner, artwork, sizing, MOQ and sampling requirements.
answer: Start with the intended wearer and training use, then specify the shell, liner, leg opening and waistband. Prepare artwork, quantities and a size breakdown, confirm the applicable MOQ and sample schedule, and approve a physical sample before bulk production.

sections.title: What should you look for in custom MMA shorts?
paragraphs: Choosing custom MMA shorts is not only a design decision. The right pair must support movement, stay secure during training, communicate your brand identity and fit your production plan. For a gym, academy, team or private-label fightwear brand, the most reliable process is to decide the use case first, then confirm construction, fabric, artwork and sizing before requesting a sample.
This guide explains the main specifications to review when developing custom MMA shorts, BJJ grappling shorts or a coordinated fightwear collection. Start with six questions:
bullets: Who will wear the shorts? Fighters, grapplers, gym members, coaches or retail customers may need different fits and features.
Where will they be used? Training, sparring, competition, team uniforms and everyday gym use can require different construction choices.
How much mobility is needed? Kicks, sprawls, guard work and clinching all place different demands on the garment.
What artwork must be included? Consider logos, sponsor marks, names, numbers, patterns and repeat-order consistency.
What quantity and size range are required? This affects the sample plan, grading and final quotation.
Which rules apply? Always check the requirements of the relevant event, federation or gym before approving a competition product.

sections.title: 2. Select fabric for movement and training comfort
paragraphs: Fabric selection should be based on the intended activity rather than appearance alone. MMA and grappling shorts commonly need a combination of stretch, light weight, drying performance and resistance to repeated washing.

A fabric specification should include composition, weight, stretch direction, finish and approved color references. Avoid approving a product from a photo alone; the fabric hand feel, opacity and stretch recovery should be checked during sampling.
bullets: Stretch: Four-way stretch can help the garment move with the athlete during kicks, sprawls and grappling exchanges.
Recovery: The fabric should return to its original shape after repeated movement instead of becoming loose.
Weight: A lightweight shell can reduce distraction during training, while a liner may use a different weight for support and coverage.
Drying performance: Quick-drying materials are useful for high-sweat training and frequent washing. Confirm the agreed performance requirements.
Opacity and coverage: This is especially important for 2-in-1 designs and light-colored artwork.
Print compatibility: Confirm whether the selected fabric produces the desired color, detail and consistency with sublimation printing.

sections.title: 3. Decide between a liner and an unlined shell
paragraphs: A liner changes the purpose and fit of the shorts. An unlined shell is often preferred when athletes want a lighter outer layer or plan to wear separate compression apparel. A 2-in-1 style combines an outer short with a close-fitting liner and can create a more complete training product.

For a private-label brand, the 2-in-1 format can also create a stronger product story because the customer is buying a defined system rather than a basic pair of shorts. It is still important to test the product through realistic movements before bulk production. When developing a lined style, confirm:
bullets: Liner length and coverage
Compression level
Seam placement
Waistband connection
Moisture management
Whether the liner rides up during movement
Whether the outer shell and liner artwork need to match

sections.title: 4. Check the waistband and closure system
paragraphs: A fight short can have excellent artwork and still fail if the waistband does not remain secure. Ask your manufacturer to explain the waistband construction and available closure options.

For competition use, hardware and closure requirements may vary by organization. Confirm the applicable rules before finalizing the design. A training product and a competition product should not automatically use the same specification.
bullets: Elastic width and recovery
Drawcord position and length
Hook-and-loop or alternative closure design, where appropriate
Inner waistband comfort
Branding or label placement
Whether the waistband works across the full size range

sections.title: 5. Use side splits and gussets to improve mobility
paragraphs: Side splits are a visible design element, but they also influence how the shorts move. A higher split may support a wider range of motion, while reinforcement is needed to keep the opening stable after repeated use.

If your design includes a gusset or additional panel, request a clear technical drawing or mockup. Small changes in panel shape can affect mobility, appearance and sewing complexity. Your specification should state:
bullets: Split height
Front and back length
Hem shape
Reinforcement method
Stitch type and thread color
Whether the split is symmetrical or asymmetric

sections.title: 6. Plan sublimation artwork for production, not just for the mockup
paragraphs: Full-color sublimation allows brands, gyms and teams to create coordinated fightwear with complex graphics. However, artwork must be prepared with production constraints in mind.

Ask for a mockup that shows the artwork on the actual garment panels. Check whether logos cross seams, splits or curved areas. Also confirm how colors will be handled across different fabrics, because the same digital color may appear different on a shell, liner or waistband.

TONTON’s custom project process is designed to align artwork, product construction, fabric direction and commercial details before sampling. This helps reduce revisions when the design moves from a screen mockup to a physical garment. Before sampling, provide:
bullets: Vector logos where available
Brand color references
Artwork at the correct scale
Authorized sponsor logos and their placement priority
Athlete names or numbers, if required
A clear front, back, side and waistband layout
Notes about labels, packaging and repeat orders

sections.title: 7. Build a practical size and quantity plan
paragraphs: A good size plan is based on the actual customer or team profile, not an equal number of every size by default. For a gym or academy, collect historical order information when possible. For a new brand, use the expected market and planned size chart as a starting point, then adjust after the first sales cycle.

For selected TONTON styles, the website states an MOQ starting from 10 pieces, while the final quantity, color breakdown and production plan are confirmed according to the brief. Treat published MOQ and sampling windows as starting points, not a substitute for a product-specific quotation. Your order brief should include:
bullets: Adult or youth sizing
Required size range
Body measurements and garment measurements
Quantity by size and color
Separate quantities for shell and 2-in-1 versions
Tolerance expectations
Packaging and labeling requirements

sections.title: 8. Approve a sample before bulk production
paragraphs: A sample should be reviewed as a product, not only as a printed sample. Test the fit and construction through movements that match the intended use: stance changes, kicks, sprawls, hip escapes, clinching and repeated squats.
Only approve bulk production after the final specification, artwork and sample comments are recorded. This creates a reference for future repeat orders. Use this approval checklist:
bullets: Is the waistband secure without uncomfortable pressure?
Does the side split support movement without opening too far?
Does the liner stay in place?
Are seams smooth and reinforced where needed?
Is the fabric opaque and comfortable after sweating?
Are logos positioned correctly on the worn garment?
Are colors acceptable under natural and indoor lighting?
Does the size chart match the approved sample?
Are labels, care instructions and packaging correct?

sections.title: Custom MMA shorts buyer checklist
paragraphs: Before requesting a quote, prepare the following information. The clearer the brief, the easier it is for a manufacturer to recommend a practical construction and provide an accurate quote.
bullets: Product type: fight shorts, side-split shorts, 2-in-1 grappling shorts or training shorts
Intended user: brand customers, gym members, athletes or teams
Estimated quantity and size breakdown
Fabric and liner preferences
Waistband and closure direction
Split, gusset and reinforcement requirements
Logo files and artwork references
Target delivery market and timing
Label, packaging and private-label requirements
Competition or organization rules, if applicable

sections.title: Final takeaway
paragraphs: The best custom MMA shorts are developed from the athlete’s movement needs, the buyer’s business model and the manufacturer’s production capability. Define the use case, choose the construction, confirm fabric and waistband details, prepare production-ready artwork, plan sizes carefully and approve a physical sample before bulk production.

For brands, gyms and teams starting a custom fightwear project, TONTON can support custom rash guards, MMA and BJJ shorts, training shorts and coordinated team kits. Begin with the product type, quantity, artwork and required timing so the next design and quotation steps can be organized around a clear brief.

faqs: Are custom MMA shorts suitable for both brands and gyms?

Yes. The same development process can support private-label brands, MMA gyms, BJJ academies, clubs and teams. The difference is usually the quantity plan, artwork system, labeling and repeat-order requirements.
What is the difference between MMA shorts and grappling shorts?

The terms can overlap, but grappling shorts often emphasize movement during ground work and may use a side split, gusset or compression liner. The best choice depends on the athlete’s movement needs and the intended training or competition rules.
Are 2-in-1 grappling shorts better than unlined shorts?

Not automatically. A 2-in-1 design can provide layered coverage and support, while an unlined shell may feel lighter and allow the wearer to choose separate compression apparel. Sample both when the target customer’s preference is uncertain.
What artwork files should I send to a manufacturer?

Send vector logos when available, brand color references, design files, placement notes and any sponsor or athlete personalization requirements. Reference images are useful, but they should be accompanied by a clear list of what must be reproduced.
How many pieces are needed to start a custom order?
The MOQ depends on the product, customization and production plan. TONTON lists selected styles from 10 pieces, with final quantity and size breakdown confirmed after reviewing the project brief.

The sampling window depends on the product, artwork and specification. TONTON lists a target sample window of 3–7 days for selected products after usable artwork and product details are confirmed. Always request a project-specific schedule.
Should I make one sample for every size?

Usually, the first approval focuses on the construction and a representative size, followed by a review of the grading and size chart. For a broad size range or a complex 2-in-1 product, additional size checks may be worthwhile.
